title: App diversity mattered more at larger synthetic tool-use training budgets
summary: Across 849 Qwen3.5 training runs, tool-use performance depended on how demonstrations were split among apps, tasks and database configurations. A composition-aware fit predicted the highest-compute quarter with mean absolute error 0.029, versus 0.171 from task count alone. A separate synthetic dataset also favored greater app diversity at its higher task budget.
ai_technology: Qwen3.5; GLM-5.2 demonstrations; nonlinear scaling regression

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 §§3.2, 4.1–4.3 and Appendix C, E.1 and E.3

evidence.tested: Across 849 SynthAPI runs, a composition-aware fit had 0.0285 mean absolute error on the highest-compute quartile versus 0.1706 for the task-count-only fit. A separate SimSAT subsampling analysis observed a switch toward higher app diversity at 1,024 versus smaller task budgets.
evidence.unknown: The full fit was validated within the SynthAPI pipeline, and the second dataset checked one app-diversity trend. Both used synthetic environments. App coverage and benchmark weighting can affect the fitted relationship.
evidence.ai_role: GLM-5.2 supplied verifier-screened synthetic tool-use episodes for supervised training of Qwen3.5 students. Performance under controlled dataset composition trained size-specific nonlinear scaling fits.
